title: Twelve Minutes
excerpt: Every extraction has a clock. This one has a debt.
content:
The pen clicked at 23:47:12, and Mara's eleven minutes started.

She had done two hundred and one extractions, and they all began the same way — a click, a clock, a door that would only be a door once. What made this one different was not the city, or the checkpoint, or the four men between her and the target.

What made it different was the name on the file.

Adeyemi, T. The man who had written the list. The man whose signature, six years ago, had turned her from a person with a passport into a ghost with a skill set. She had rehearsed this moment on three continents, and in every rehearsal she walked away.

The clock said otherwise. The money said otherwise. And somewhere below her, in a basement that existed on no survey map, the man himself was waiting for the extraction he had paid for — from the only fixer alive stubborn enough to take it.

Mara went over the wall at 23:49:03.

The first guard was simple. The second was careful. The third had a dog, and the dog had opinions, and by the time she had finished explaining them quietly, the clock read 23:55.

Six minutes to get down two floors, through a service corridor, past a man whose face she knew better than her own.

She found him exactly where the file said she would: sitting calmly, hands visible, a man being extracted who looked like he had written the extraction himself. Because he had. He'd written hers, too.

"Mara," Adeyemi said, like six years was a long weekend. "You brought the good bolt cutters."

"Four minutes," she said.

"Then we should talk fast," he said, "because the list you've been running from? It's not a list of people I burned. It's a list of people I'm about to save — and your name is next."
